name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+17 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Deborah Ross has a decisive fundraising edge ($1.97M raised, $1.36M on hand; no challenger funds reported)
Prediction markets price Democratic victory near 99 percent
No general-election polls or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 17-point Democratic lean, Ross's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing her win at about 99 percent all point in the same direction, with no evidence of a competitive challenge from Eugene Douglass.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Ross or unexpectedly strong challenger fundraising could narrow the margin, though hardly enough to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Carolina's 2nd District is a strongly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points toward Democrats. Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election after clearing her primary and faces Republican Eugene Douglass along with a Libertarian candidate in the general election. No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Ross holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised about $2 million with $1.4 million on hand, while no challenger fundraising has been reported. Prediction markets price her chances at roughly 99 percent. The combination of the district's lean, her incumbency, and the absence of any reported challenger activity points to a comfortable Democratic win; the realistic uncertainty concerns the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
